x: Eyebrows were raised when it was noticed that Bill Dance, usually only too keen to take on suicidally fast starts, was taking things more steadily in company with Gerry North and not far from our newly joined Guardsman Dick Piotrowski.
Laurie O'Hara tagged him closely but Fairclough was nearly caught napping and took half a lap to close up again, whilst Dick Piotrowski failed to get out of the ruck in time to maintain contact.

Dick Piotrowski making his debut for us on the road and his first outing as a first claim member fully justified his 'A' team selection just beating our old friend Mel Thorpe (Coventry G)--our second man home in 1966.

With Mel Thorpe's departure to Coventry Godiva Harriers we were doubly pleased to welcome Dick Piotrowski to our ranks. Dick, formerly a member of Bracknell AC, is stationed with the Guards at Chelsea Barracks (just local to ur training tracks at Battersea and the Duke of York's) and has become firs…
Dick Piotrowski held second place and although John Dear dropped to 6th on stage three they were still ahead of the 'A' outfit despite fine recovery efforts by Bill Dance and Gerry North.

Dick Piotrowski, a new member and running his first road relay for the club was on stage 7 and here again inexperience was soon apparent and he had to relinquish our 5th place to Reading who in every race are striving to beat us.

Bill Dance "relegated" to the 'B' team on this occasion, succeeded in putting the selectors to shame by soundly beating 'A' team runner Dick Piotrowski, albeit having only his second outing for us on the road.

Having won this race last year it was necessary this time to find a completely new team and with Dick Piotrowski, John Dear, Roger Donnison, Lionel Mann, Malcolm Simms, Howard Satchell, Bob Glover and Pat O'Connor eligible we appeared to have a strong team but unfortunately Donnison, Mann, Simms and…

In fact their last minute timing (not for the first time!) prompted the question as to whether Don McLean's 'title' was in jeopardy!!.It was good to see steeple-chasers John Bicourt and Dick Piotrowski out on the road, at what is a slightly longer than usual distance for them,as well as being a tough race.
In the Berkshire Championships at Maidenhead DICK PIOTROWSKI split the Stevens brothers of Reading AC to finish an excellent 2nd. Meredith and Merriman, also of Reading, were a minute down.

Our bright young prospects, Dick Piotrowski and Cliff Calderwood pulled off the Club 10 miles and 5 miles championships respectively and impressed the onlookers with a brand of running that holds a bright future for both.
Well, the whole team got a good start with Dick Piotrowski showing good form these days, well to the fore closely followed by John Bicourt and Peter Whewell, both surely destined for the first 10?

Belgrave eyes were focussed on the men of unknown form, Dick Piotrowski and Trevor Hart. Both ran well above expectations (it was Trevor's first race since last winter) and were our fourth and fifth scorers - things looked good for 1968.
John Bicourt looks favourite, but just how far behind him John Dear, Bill Dance and Dick Piotrowski are when it comes to selection remains to be seen.
Our other winner of the day was Dick Piotrowski who took the 3000 metres steeplechase in a personal best time of 9:09.0 - watch out Bicourt!!!

Dick Piotrowski continued his run of good form and was 24 seconds faster than last year. Others to show great improvement in 12 months were John Hall (58 secs), Bill Laws (56 secs) and Pat O'Connor (34secs).

A small but select pack detached themselves from the main field round the first lap of the common with Pat O'Connor, Dick Piotrowski, Trevor Hart, Alan Black and a new member from New Zealand, Kelly Diprose, prominent.

Dick Piotrowski was on Stage 7 and although staying in 5th place dropped away from the leaders. Ernie Earl that old battler for Hercules was in great form and took his club into the lead once more and following him was a fight between Coventry, Poly and Manchester which resulted in Poly taking 2nd p…

Dick Piotrowski, from whom we had expected a good run, also started well but fell back slowly throughout the race and was disappointing. Patrick O'Connor, Lionel Mann and John Dear ran well and Tony Brien in his first major race for us showed he is a new member with considerable promise.
Dick Piotrowski learnt a lesson from the Inter Counties and the South of Thames and ran his best race to date for us by finding his early pace admirably.
He made an impact last December when he finished up amongst our senior first team men in the Club '7', taking the handicap as well, and beating John Dear and Dick Piotrowski.
Dick Piotrowski faded, as he is wont to do when he starts too fast, but Lionel Mann made up for it by the opposite approach. Bill Dance and Trevor Hart both ran to current form.

: (Ron Linstead) BELGRAVE take "Silver" in the National Relay at Leicester, and here is Trevor Hart handing over to Dick Piotrowski at the end of stage 8, in third place and 47 seconds behind the ultimate winners, Coventry Godiva.
STAGE 10: Dick Piotrowski (15:40---1st fastest) Dick became our third consecutive fastest man for the short stage and brought us back to within 21 seconds of the leaders.

Next came Dick Piotrowski and although gaining a little on Tipton dropped five seconds on Coventry. The race was now in its last stages and we still had four excellent runners to come with a trump card for the last stage but we had reckoned without Dick Taylor.
With Dick Piotrowski and Alan Black also well under 10 minutes and John Dear , recovered from a nasty injury, capable of 9-30 or under, we look strong.

Another impressive performance came in the steeplechase where Peter Morris moved smoothly to a personal best ahead of Dick Piotrowski. Lionel Mann ran his obligatory second race of the day and showed the most unorthodox jump technique since the balmy days of Arkle.
Before the end of a mile, Peter had opened up a small gap from Tony Fairclough and then four runners, Lionel Mann, John Dear, Dick Piotrowski and Laurie O'Hara followed.

Our strongest representation was in the 3,000 metres steeplechase where we had John Bicourt Peter Morris and Dick Piotrowski. The latter two just failed to qualify for the final (Peter by the proverbial whisker) and clocked 8:59.0 and 9:03.8 respectively.
Peter is our 5,000 metres champion and his steeplechasing prowess brings one to those other two top form 'chasers John Bicourt and Dick Piotrowski who have both had their best ever summer seasons.
John Bicourt continued his steady improvement and it was encouraging to see Peter Morris and Dick Piotrowski (despite a nasty mid-season injury) not far behind.
Dick Piotrowski on Stage 7 was not in the least deterred by the closeness of Hercules and proceeded to open up a gap of 63 secs which later in the race proved invaluable.

Stage 1.- An early lead, which they were never to lose, for City of Stoke (S.Hope 12:52) with Ealing and Southall second (P.Fagin 13:01) and our own Dick Piotrowski (13:03) doing our second fastest time of the day for third place.

On leaving the Common,Geoff was five seconds clear with Dick Piotrowski showing up well, just ahead of the following bunch. At the bottom of Copse Hill the leader had stretched the gap to 15 seconds ahead of brother Gerry and Dick who were in turn 15 seconds clear of the next six.

The almost spring like conditions, very firm going, (most unusual on this course), and the possible shortening of the course explained why no less than seven runners broke Gerry North's record (12:40 in 1968) as well as being equalled by Lionel Mann and Dick Piotrowski.
DICK PIOTROWSKI was placed 7th in the Wolverton '5' on November 29th finishing 75secs down on winner Ron Grove and 23 seconds behind Luton's Tony Simmons.

Dick Piotrowski and Lionel Mann provided excellent backing in 15th and 19th places respectively, enabling us to take second place in the team race to the consistently strong Hercules Wimbledon outfit.

Dick Piotrowski suffered a family bereavement at the beginning of February and naturally found it difficult to put much into his running; but he is now going great guns and showing his best ever form.

For the climb up Cambridge Road it was Smith, O'Hara, Mann and Piotrowski leading the field leaving the final scene to be enacted over the last lap of the common where a 'return to form' Dick Piotrowski outsprinted fast finisher Laurie O'Hara.

The net result was that John handed over to Dick Piotrowski 11 seconds in arrears. This stage saw a 5 second improvement in our position, but Medway had displaced Reading, so Dick's run had brought us almost to the lead which was well and truly established on the next stage by Bill Kerr who led the…

Dick Piotrowski then led in the rest of our crowd with some impressive looking packing but unfortunately with only three to score even this was not good enough to give us first place, although our second position was an improvement on former years.

John Bicourt is already well under 9 minutes and it is good to see Alan Black and Dick Piotrowski back in action again after injury. A word of encouragement to such as Nigel Bacon, who has deputised for others absent on innumerable occasions- keep plugging away, Mate, we need you!
